pr_title: preserve resource private data on error
pr_body:
If the provider returns an empty response during apply, we restore the
prior state for the resource, but the private data was not being
restored.

Fixes #27452

provider "aws" {

### Expected Behavior
`terraform destroy` after the initial one should respect the aws_subnet custom deletion timeout.

### Actual Behavior
`terraform destroy` after the initial one does not respect the aws_subnet custom deletion timeout.

### Steps to Reproduce
<!--
Please list the full steps required to reproduce the issue, for example:
1. `terraform init`
2. `terraform apply`

1. `terraform apply`

```
$ terraform apply -var-file=creds.tfvars

aws_vpc.vpc: Creating...
aws_vpc.vpc: Creation complete after 6s [id=vpc-1234]
aws_subnet.subnet: Creating...
aws_subnet.subnet: Creation complete after 1s [id=subnet-1234]

Apply complete! Resources: 2 added, 0 changed, 0 destroyed.
```

Ensure that in the `terraform.tfstate` the subnet contains:

```
            "timeouts": {
              "create": "5m",
              "delete": "5m"
            },
```

2. Add a dependency that blocks the deletion of the subnet

For example launch a sample ec2 instance that use the vpc and subnet from above. Our goal is to have a dependent resource that would block the subnet deletion.

comments:
Thanks for confirming this in 0.14 @ialidzhikov.
It appears that terraform is not restoring the saved timeout information when the provider doesn't return a state with that timeout error.

@jbardin , thank you for looking into this issue and providing the fix so quickly, appreciate it! I would really love to see this bug fix cherry-picked into v0.14, v0.13 and v0.12 (if it is possible, of course).
Hi @ialidzhikov, sorry but in this case the PR does not directly apply to older versions.
Hmm, you mean that the code path in the older versions is different compared to the master branch and it is not easy to cherry-pick the PR?

That is correct. The bug does not represent a regression in 0.14, nor a blocker to upgrade, so it will be included in the next major release. Versions prior to 0.14 are no longer under active development.

I'm going to lock this issue because it has been closed for _30 days_ ⏳. This helps our maintainers find and focus on the active issues.

If you have found a problem that seems similar to this, please open a new issue and complete the issue template so we can capture all the details necessary to investigate further.

review_comments: What happens if the object was tainted? Should this be `newState.Status`?

James pointed out what I was missing in slack:
> newStatus is only set to tainted if the the value is null, but then only assigned if the value is not null

`newStatus` could only be set to `ObjectTainted` is `newVal` is null, but this requires that `newVal` is not null so it would never be set; so there is no change in behavior here.

I do think that we may lose the `ObjectTainted` status if a provider errors when removing a tainted object _and_ returns a non-null value. Most providers wouldn't be capable of doing this right now, but I'll make sure it's covered in another PR.
